summary: Both hypotheses confirmed: the greedy + simulated annealing (SA) approach scored 81.61 out of 100, while the greedy-only baseline scored 46.76, demonstrating that SA nearly doubles the score and is essential for competitive performance on this rectangle packing optimization problem.
key_points: h-main (greedy + SA) scored 81.61, exceeding the predicted threshold of 80.
h-control-negative (greedy only) scored 46.76, far below the predicted ceiling of 70 — the 34.85-point gap is larger than the expected ~15+ points, confirming SA is the dominant improvement driver.

SA nearly doubles the score over greedy placement alone (81.61 vs 46.76), meaning future iterations should focus on improving SA parameters, move operators, or initial solution quality rather than the greedy heuristic.

Score of 81.61 leaves ~18 points of potential improvement; next steps could include tuning SA temperature schedule, trying different neighborhood moves (e.g., rectangle swaps, boundary adjustments), or exploring alternative approaches like constraint-based partitioning.
